paragraphs.text: Good evening, sisters and elders. What a beautiful day it's been. I hope you got a little of that rain that we enjoyed down here in our part of the mission. You know, when we first came to the Philippines, it seemed like it rained every day. And I loved it because I love the rain. But lately it seems like there hasn't been that much rain. And so today was just fantastic. I went outside, I smelled it up. You know, I just really love the smell of the rain. I love what the rain does, cleanses and nourishes nature. And you know, I'm just thankful for the rain. Okay, enough about me and rain.

Are you using some of the time you have each morning to write down four or five things that you're grateful for? If not, you're missing out on one of the best ways to make yourself truly happy. Happiness is a choice for sure. But gratitude is a lever that makes the happiness choice easy to make. Please give it a try if you're not already doing it. And if you are already doing it, keep it up. Life is gonna be what it's gonna be. And we can either learn from it, grow from it and be happy in it or not. It's our choice.

As Shakespeare wrote in his play Hamlet, "there is nothing either good or bad but thinking makes it so." I think what Shakespeare was trying to tell us is that maybe, just maybe, everything that happens to us can be turned to good. And we know why that is because of the atonement of Jesus Christ. In fact, do a little mind experiment with me. Have you ever had a bad experience that a few months or years later turned out to be one of the most important experiences of your life? Think about it. I have many times. And so have many others.

In fact, it is so common in our lives that there's a story about it in almost every culture. I've heard this story as though from a Chinese peasant. I've heard it as though from a Japanese Zen monk. And recently I heard it again as an Arabic folk story. It goes like this. This is the Arabic version.

There was once a wise old man whose son went to the well one day when it was very hot. In fact, it was at its most extreme. He was the only one at the well. To his surprise, he found a beautiful, tame, black, Arabian horse there. Everyone in the village envied the young man and he started to win all the races with his new horse. The villagers told the old man, your boy is blessed with good luck, good fortune, to which the old man responded, you never know for sure. A week later, the boy fell off the horse and broke his legs. So they rushed to the old man and said, your boy's good luck has turned bad. To which he responded, you never really know for sure. A week later, a rival village suddenly attacked and all the able and healthy young men were drafted and many were killed. Because the son's legs were broken, he was spared. And so it was again and again with the old man saying, you never really know for sure.

Here we are called to serve our missions when the whole world is experiencing a deadly pandemic. And we're on a strict lockdown and can't do a lot of the normal activities we thought we'd be doing as missionaries. People might say, wow, you're really unlucky. And we can honestly reply, you never really know for sure.

Elders and sisters, what I do know for sure is that no righteous effort is ever wasted. And everything you do that helps and uplifts another person will be answered upon your own life in due time. So I can promise to you just what the prophet Alma promised his son in Alma 41, verse 14. "Therefore my son, see that ye are merciful unto your brethren, deal justly, judge righteously, and do good continually. And if you do all these things, then shall ye receive your reward. Ye shall have mercy restored unto you again. You shall have justice restored unto you again. Ye shall have a righteous judgment restored unto you again. And ye shall have good rewarded unto you again." And then when this is all over, you'll be able to say, "the greatest growth and service I experienced in the mission field happened during the lockdown. I was so blessed."

Good night, elders and sisters. Hope you have a sleep well. And looking forward to zone conference tomorrow, other district conferences tomorrow for the Bulacan Zone. And then, of course, we'll go right to the rest of the mission. We're excited about it, excited for what we're going to share and what you're going to share back with us. God bless you. We love you. Good night.
